subject: Re: Concurrency & Rate Limits — Redwood performance qualification
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: concurrency & rate limit details / next steps

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from today’s discovery on performance/SLOs and concurrency. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary of targets you shared:
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 200 ms for our interactive UI (typical prompt sizes: 60-120 tokens).
- Throughput: Peak sustained ingress during business hours ~ 600 requests/minute (~10 RPS), bursty peaks up to ~600 RPS for short windows (1-2 minutes) during events.
- Concurrency: ~120 concurrent active requests at peak (this is from connection pooling across many browser clients; per-user concurrent requests ~2-3).
- Streaming: UI requires token streaming (SSE) for assistant responses; 1-2 concurrent streams per active session is typical.

Open questions we flagged on the call:
- Is the 120 concurrent requests estimate global across your app or per-region? (I think global but you’ll confirm.)
- Are there long-running requests that hold the connection >30s (e.g., >1k token generations)?

Immediate asks / proposed next steps:
1) Can you confirm the concurrency is global and not per-region? (If per-region, please share expected distribution.)
2) Please send any traffic sample (CSV) showing requests/min by minute for a recent 24-72 hour period -- helps us tune batching and KV cache policies.
3) We can propose an initial quota bump for the pilot (see attached "concurrency_calc.xlsx" + Redwood rate limits deck). Suggested trial: 500 RPS quota with soft auto-throttle and a rollback policy if error rate exceeds 1.5%.
4) Internal: I’ll loop in Nikhil to provide recommended connection-pooling and backoff settings for your front-end and API layer.

Attachments: concurrency_calc.xlsx (calculated concurrency scenarios), redwood-rate-limits.pdf (summary of default limits and bump options).

If that plan looks good I’ll send a short email to your SRE with the formal quota request and a mutually agreed pilot timeframe (2-4 weeks).

Thanks -- Marissa

Alex -- thanks for the fast turnaround. Short answers below and a formal proposal to follow.

How Redwood models limits:
- We have two complimentary controls: "RPS quota" (requests per second) for ingress shaping, and a "concurrent inference token" budget that maps more directly to GPU concurrency for heavy models/long sequences. For interactive UIs we typically size both so that RPS handles short bursts and concurrent tokens cover sustained parallelism.

Mapping suggestion for your case (based on the numbers you shared):
- Pilot quota: 500 RPS (soft) across NA with a 2% rate-limit headroom.
- Concurrent token budget: reserve for ~150 concurrent inference slots (this maps to the 120 concurrent requests plus buffer for system overhead).
- Streaming: no additional quota for SSE; streaming is accounted in token consumption and connection slots. We’ll enable streaming-optimized batching for your pilot.

Pricing/Procurement note: I’ll attach a short addendum to the MSA with a temporary quota override for the pilot and a rollback SLA that we can use during the 2-4 week pilot. That will include an explicit error-rate threshold (1.5%) and an escalation path.

Next steps I’ll take now:
- Share formal quota proposal and price addendum (HubSpot deal updated: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567).
- Request quota increase from our infra team (DocuSign/procurement links will be included in the proposal).

Nikhil / Dev -- can you confirm the recommended client-side pooling/backoff and a simple curl example we can pass to their SRE for testing?

Thanks -- Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: concurrency & rate limit details / next steps

Looping in with technical recommendations -- forwarding key points and a minimal test snippet.

Recommended connection-pooling and client settings:
- Keep-alive: 60s (increase from 30s to reduce TLS handshakes at scale)
- Max connections per host: 200 (given UI distributes across many clients, this helps avoid head-of-line blocking)
- HTTP/2 where possible: multiplexing reduces per-connection concurrency pressure
- Backoff policy: expo-backoff with jitter, initial 100ms, max 2s, retry limit 3 for idempotent requests
- Streaming: use chunked transfer / SSE client with a 5s heartbeat to detect stalls; close idle streams after 30s of inactivity.

Simple test (curl) to simulate concurrent streaming requests:
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=gpt-redwood-1&stream=true"

We’ll also provide a small k6 script to simulate your 120 concurrent streams and ramp to 500 RPS. Marissa -- let me know if you want the script attached to the proposal.

On quotas: we can provision a soft 500 RPS/150 concurrent-slot pilot for 2-4 weeks while monitoring error rate and latency. If you need a faster response-time SLO (p50/p95 tighter than 200ms), we may recommend a larger reserved concurrency pool or pinning to a dedicated capacity instance.

-Nikhil
